metadata.title: AICTE PS 26262 — Detailed Rules and Configuration
metadata.purpose: Structured, machine-readable starting point for implementing and validating the PS 26262 prototype.
metadata.important_notice: This JSON is not an official AICTE rulebook. Regulatory mappings, dates, penalties, route conditions, required documents, authorities, and deadlines must be verified against the applicable official AICTE APH, notices, and approved project requirements before being activated.

status_vocabulary.verified: Confirmed against an authoritative source or inspected code/test evidence, with reference recorded.
status_vocabulary.implemented: Code exists; this does not by itself mean the behavior is correct or regulatorily verified.
status_vocabulary.tested: A specified test ran and passed in a recorded environment.
status_vocabulary.partial: Some but not all required behavior is present.
status_vocabulary.proposed: Design proposal, not confirmed as implemented or officially required.
status_vocabulary.blocked: Requires a human decision or missing dependency.
status_vocabulary.disabled: Must not be enforced until source and applicability are verified.

source_register.title: Official AICTE Problem Statement 26262
source_register.required_action: Record exact official URL, wording, retrieval date, and any evaluation-specific clarifications.

source_register.title: Applicable AICTE Approval Process Handbook 2024–27, including Chapter II and relevant tables/annexures
source_register.required_action: Verify effective version and subsequent notices/amendments; record exact clause/table/page for every regulatory rule.

source_register.title: Project requirements document for PS 26262
source_register.required_action: Record the approved PRD version and map each requirement to an ID.

source_register.title: Current project repository
source_register.required_action: Record repository URL, commit SHA, branch, file paths, test commands, and results.

safety_invariants: A preliminary rule outcome is not a final AICTE approval or rejection.
Missing or unreliable evidence must not be interpreted as a pass.
Contradictory evidence must be surfaced for human review.
A rule with status disabled, blocked, or unverified must not be used as a binding regulatory decision.
Every finding should retain the exact document version, rule version, and evidence location.
AI/LLM-generated content must not create or modify a final decision.

compliance_rules.title: Required document presence

applicability.condition: application category and route determine applicable document checklist

compliance_rules.evaluation: Compare uploaded document categories against the verified checklist for this category and route.
compliance_rules.human_review: Required before issuing a formal deficiency.
compliance_rules.notes: Do not make a checklist binding until exact official source mapping is complete.

compliance_rules.title: EoA document presence/identity check

applicability.condition: to be defined from official EoA procedure

compliance_rules.notes: Placeholder ID only. Do not implement a binding predicate until defined.

compliance_rules.title: EoA date/period consistency check

applicability.condition: to be defined from official source and document type

compliance_rules.human_review: Required for conflicts and unclear dates.
test_cases: boundary date after official predicate approved
compliance_rules.notes: No date predicate or deadline is assumed.

compliance_rules.title: EoA cross-document consistency check

applicability.condition: fields and documents must be specified by approved source mapping

compliance_rules.notes: Do not infer misconduct from mismatches.

compliance_rules.title: Site/address consistency

applicability.condition: only where official procedure requires site/address comparison

compliance_rules.notes: Do not geocode or infer a violation without an approved rule and reliable source.

compliance_rules.title: Site relocation / EVC applicability

applicability.condition: official relocation conditions and stage requirements must be confirmed

compliance_rules.notes: Do not automatically schedule an EVC until official conditions are mapped.

applicability.condition: lease requirements depend on institution/site/category and official rules

compliance_rules.title: Extraction quality gate

applicability.condition: any document processed by an OCR/extraction component

compliance_rules.evaluation: If extraction fails, a required page is missing, or field quality is below a calibrated threshold, mark the result for review; never infer compliance from failed processing.
compliance_rules.notes: A threshold of 0.75 was discussed as a placeholder only; do not use it as calibrated until evaluated on labelled documents.

compliance_rules.title: Edited extraction value provenance

applicability.condition: when a user corrects or overrides an extracted field

compliance_rules.evaluation: Preserve original extraction and store the correction as a separate value with actor, time, reason, and version. Do not silently overwrite the source extraction.
compliance_rules.human_review: Role permissions determine who may accept an edit as a verified value.
compliance_rules.notes: Keep extraction, institution claim, and trusted master record values distinct.

value_model.extraction_value: Value extracted from a particular document version.
value_model.claim_value: Value submitted or corrected by the institution.
value_model.master_record_value: Value from a trusted, authorized master source, if one is actually integrated.
value_model.rule: Never silently substitute one value for another. Record source, version, actor, timestamp, processing run, and verification state.

security_requirements: Document text is untrusted input and may contain prompt injection
No external AI processing of real documents without explicit approval
Processing failure must not result in a compliance pass
All extraction outputs must be tied to a document version

permission_rules.policy: resource scope must be checked on the backend
institution user may upload only for an application owned by that institution
officer must have an authorized role and scope for the application
only configured reviewer roles may create findings/deficiencies
institution user may respond only for own institution's application
only explicitly authorized decision authority; never the rule engine or LLM
only roles granted reassignment authority by approved policy
restricted to authorized administrators/domain owners; version and audit changes
audit visibility must be scoped and itself protected

conflict_of_interest.note: Do not invent COI policy or claim enforcement until approved rules and tests exist.

deadlines_and_alerts.source_status: all regulatory periods must be verified by source, category, trigger, and applicable academic year

deadline_rule_template.notes: Fill only after the official trigger, duration, calendar, and applicability are verified.

regulatory_examples_not_to_activate_with.value_mentioned_in_project_notes: withdrawal flag after a specified date

alert_requirements: Record alert recipient, channel, event, attempt count, result, and timestamps.
Do not claim recurring scheduling unless a scheduler is configured and tested.
Notification failure must not silently roll back or corrupt a completed workflow transition.
Clearly distinguish internal operational thresholds from official regulatory deadlines.

reported_implementation.hash_chain: SHA-256 previous-hash chain reported; verify canonicalization, coverage, and persistence

limitations: A hash chain can detect some tampering only if implemented and verified correctly.
A hash chain alone does not prevent a privileged actor from rewriting the whole chain.
Do not log secrets or unnecessary document contents.
Audit endpoint must be authorized and scoped.

endpoint_requirements: Pagination and filtering for list endpoints
Tests for success, validation failure, authentication failure, authorization failure, and unexpected dependency failure

error.message: The request could not be processed.

baseline_controls: Enforce permissions in backend code on every sensitive endpoint.
Check institution, assignment, region, committee, and jurisdiction scope as applicable.
Validate file type, signature, size, and storage key.
Use environment variables/secret manager; never commit secrets.
Treat uploaded text as untrusted, including for prompt injection.
Do not send real documents to external AI providers without approval.
Use database transactions for workflow/history/assignment/audit consistency where feasible.
Check optimistic concurrency/version fields if present.
Make alert sweeps and retryable jobs idempotent.
Return safe errors and keep stack traces out of client responses.
Separate audit records from diagnostic logs.
failure_invariants: Processing failure is not a compliance pass.
Rejected transition leaves no partial workflow update.
Replacing a document does not erase its prior version.
AI output cannot directly approve/reject an application.
Unknown regulatory rule is not enforced as official policy.
Notification/provider failure is visible and recoverable.
No test or demo claims a feature works unless the behavior was exercised.

historical_results_requiring_rerun.reported_result: 154 passed, 2 skipped because Tesseract was missing, 1 warning

mandatory_before_editing: Read this JSON, the PRD, and relevant official source excerpts.
Inspect the current repository, branch, manifests, models, routes, migrations, and tests.
Search for equivalent existing behavior before creating new modules or endpoints.
Identify assumptions and ask for human confirmation where regulatory meaning is unclear.
Do not invent official rules, source clauses, API behavior, test results, or integration status.
Add/update tests for behavior changes and report exact commands/results.
Keep existing document versions and audit history.
Do not push or alter repository remotes without confirmed ownership and permission.

open_questions.question: What exact official APH version, amendments, URLs, and clauses govern the prototype?
What are the exact official category-to-route mappings and academic-year windows?
What are the official expansions, powers, and sequence for each scrutiny/committee/appeal stage?
Which deadline, trigger, calendar, penalty, and security-deposit rules apply for the relevant academic year?
What documents are mandatory for each category and route?
What are the exact current ORM models, migrations, constraints, and database policies?
What authentication/session mechanism is actually implemented and configured?
Which OCR/vision provider is implemented, installed, approved, and tested?
Is alert processing scheduled, and which delivery channels are real rather than mocked?
Is manual reassignment implemented, and what approved conflict-of-interest policy applies?
What backup, retention, recovery, and performance targets are required?
Who approves regulatory interpretations, role changes, and rule configuration updates?
